1012	**Query.** The twenty closed operations remain read-only. The current schema is
1013	`workflows/schemas/evaluator3/graph-query.schema.json` major 3. The incorporated
1014	[query projection contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/workflows/query-projection-contract.v3.md)
1015	owns the complete selection, endpoint, result, ordering, traversal, continuation
1016	and evidence-disclosure laws for `graph.neighbors`, `graph.path` and `graph.reach`.
1017	It does not replace the artifact-specific owners of the other seventeen operations.
1018	
1019	Graph requests may select `run3`, `snapshot2` or `latest`; before traversal they
1020	resolve to one concrete retained Run and an exact fact-view selection. An empty
1021	resolver domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`; ambiguity is a typed refusal. A graph
1022	response never echoes an unresolved `latest` alias as its resolved view. Endpoint
1023	identity includes the selected universe and native identity, so equal paths in
1024	different analysis universes cannot silently collapse. Results retain their fact
1025	provenance. Database row IDs and backend iteration order are not public identity
1026	or ordering rules.
1027	
1028	The bounded graph contract distinguishes a page boundary from exhaustion of the
1029	logical operation. Page size is at most 1,000; produced items at most 100,000;
1030	semantic depth at most 64; visited nodes at most 1,000,000. `maxDepth` defines the
1031	requested search distance, not an implicit promise of unbounded reachability.
1032	`completeness=required` refuses genuinely unfinished work at an operation bound
1033	with `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3); exactly reaching a limit with no owed work is
1034	not incompleteness. Best-effort reports any truncation explicitly. A continuation
1035	can page only the bounded result and never reset the work budget; its last page
1036	can remain truncated with no cursor. Total-count disclosure distinguishes an
1037	exact total from a lower bound.
1038	
1039	A continuation binds the project, concrete retained Run and fact views,
1040	operation, effective parameters, ordering and position. Publication of a newer
1041	Run cannot change that selection. Index loss permits rebuilding from the same
1042	available closure; unavailable retained evidence or incompatible continuation
1043	inputs cause the contract's typed refusal, never a switch to a newer Run.
1044	
1045	For the graph operations, traversal completion and retained evidence sufficiency
1046	are separate typed disclosures, including relevant Coverage, scope, deficiency
1047	and resolution limitations. Exhausting stored edges, returning no rows, or
1048	ending pagination cannot itself prove that no callers exist. Any such finding
1049	must retain the existing native/evaluator authority and citations. All query
1050	responses carry their owned view, evidence disclosure, availability and `advisory`;

1051	the other seventeen operations retain their existing Coverage field. `advisory` is
1052	true exactly for `comparison.diff`, `candidate.list`, `inspection.show` and
1053	`review.brief`. The three graph operations are not advisory and do not seal a Run.
1054	
1055	The query command's required parity fields are `resolved-view`, `availability`,
1056	`truncated`, `total-items`, `termination-class` and `query-response`. The last is
1057	the **complete owner-admitted GraphQueryResponseV1**, including the full context,
1058	items and any optional termination; human, JSON and agent renderers preserve its
1059	typed content. For non-graph operations the existing Coverage field stays inside
1060	that response. Graph evidence is not reduced to a synthetic Coverage scalar.
1061	The first four scalar fields are exact projections of the response context;
1062	`termination-class` comes from the enclosing command's actual StepTermination.
1063	If the response carries termination, its entire object must equal the enclosing
1064	termination. The envelope and response must identify the same project. Missing
1065	required query disclosure follows the existing required-delivery fault law.
1066	
1067	The envelope's compact `QueryResult` remains a separate record. For graph.*,
1068	`items` is the number of rows on the current page, `truncated` equals the context
1069	flag, `advisory` is false, and `nextCursor` is present exactly when the context
1070	has the identical token. `completenessMet` is true exactly when `countBasis=exact`:
1071	the declared stored-edge operation has completed, even if further pages remain
1072	to be delivered. This is neither native closed-world evidence nor a claim that
1073	all pages were delivered. A lower-bound result therefore has
1074	`completenessMet=false`, including an intermediate page whose `truncated` flag
1075	is false. The other seventeen operations retain their owned summary semantics.
1076	The reference `workflows/query_surface_projection.v3.py` checks these joins and

1079	**Doctor.** `opensip doctor` produces a typed report over closures, trust, store,
1080	platform, project marker and the offline window. A produced report is `success` (0)
1081	even when defects are found (detail `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`); CI must inspect
1082	`doctor.defectsFound`. Only an unproducible report is `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (4).
1083	
1084	A `doctor` report is a **different invocation** and therefore cannot deliver the
1085	absences of an analysis invocation; `DoctorResult.defects[]` remains the

1088	**Release-availability absence rides the invocation that selected it.**
1089	`CommandEnvelope.availability` (`CapabilityAvailabilityV1` =
1090	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`, each step
1091	`CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1` = `{stepId, noticeCount, notices[]}`) carries
1092	every capability the selected product requires (native §1.4) that this release
1093	did not declare available, for **every requested unit of every analysis step** —
1094	a single-step command projects one step, and a named multi-step invocation
1095	projects one entry per analysis step that made a selection. Each notice carries the complete ownership tuple in **typed
1096	fields** — `capabilityId`, `languageMode`, `workspaceRoot` — with the existing
1097	code `native.capability-unavailable` (a `const`, since the record declares one
1098	condition); the tuple is never concatenated into a `subject`, because
1099	`workspaceRoot` is a `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024
1100	and a truncated path would collapse two distinct units into one indistinguishable
1101	notice. The collection is composed **per step** —
1102	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`, each step
1103	`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}` — because 1024 is the
1104	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and *not* an invocation-wide one: two
1105	admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices, and no notice is
1106	discarded to fit. A step that made no selection contributes no entry, a step that
1107	found nothing absent contributes an empty entry, and the same tuple may recur in

1110	Envelope membership alone would **not** deliver it: `render` selects a command's
1111	declared `parityFields`, so `capability-availability` is a declared parity field
1112	of **every** `requestClass: analysis` command — `default`, `analyze`, `fit`,
1113	`audit` and `repair-verify` — and every applicable renderer carries it: human,

1116	whose invocation selected nothing supplies the explicit empty collection
1117	(`{stepCount: 0, totalNoticeCount: 0, steps: []}`) rather than omitting the

1119	above, never a successful partial rendering.
1120	
1121	It is **advisory** — it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control

1136	
1137	Exit codes are the existing table: success 0, policy-failed 1, request-rejected 2,
1138	indeterminate 3, operational-failed 4, interrupted 130. Termination branch contract
1139	(schema-enforced): success carries no error/reason/signal; policy-failed carries
1140	`runId` or `authority=ephemeral`; request-rejected/operational-failed carry
1141	`errorCode` (operational also a non-none `faultCause` from the observation:
1142	host-io, ledger-busy, ledger-corrupt, cas-link, provider-protocol, durability-commit,
1143	delivery-required, output-serialization, extension-install-io, serve-protocol,
1144	host-invariant);
1145	indeterminate carries `reasonCodes`; interrupted carries `signal` and a `runId` only
1146	when a Run was committed before the interrupt. `DomainDetailCode` is explanatory
1147	detail beside an existing code, never a termination code. Selected goldens (the complete retained set
1148	is in the inventory and exercised by the model):
1149	
1150	| Situation | Class / exit | Code | Detail / remedy |
1151	|---|---|---|---|
1152	| fresh project, providers installed | success 0 | — | DEFAULTED durable retention disclosed; no policy file written |
1153	| required provider closure not installed | indeterminate 3 | `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | `COMPONENT.REQUIRED_CLOSURE_NOT_INSTALLED` → `opensip install provider-typescript` |
1154	| installed closure bytes corrupt / unspawnable | operational-failed 4 | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` | `DELIVERY.CLOSURE_BYTES_CORRUPT` / `DELIVERY.CLOSURE_UNSPAWNABLE` → `opensip doctor` |
1155	| selected renderer fails after commit | operational-failed 4 | `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` | `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`; runId retained |
1156	| optional export sink fails | success 0 | — | egress never changes a verdict |
1157	| `--ephemeral` with baseline/repair prerequisite | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` | `WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY` |
1158	| pivot closure missing / revoked / unmapped project | indeterminate 3 | `BASELINE.RECIPE_UNSUPPORTED` | `BASELINE.PIVOT_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE` / `..._CLOSURE_REVOKED` / `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` |
1159	| required evidence lost in audit | indeterminate 3 | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | `COMPARISON.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE` → re-import |
1160	| unmapped / corrupt import artifact | request-rejected 2 | `CONFIG.INVALID` | `IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED` / `IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT` |
1161	| duplicate waiver / imperative policy key | request-rejected 2 | `CONFIG.INVALID` | `POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER` / `POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED` |
1162	| repair preimage mismatch / source moved | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` |
1163	| recovery blocked | operational-failed 4 | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` | `REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`; journal retained |

1165	| doctor report with defects | success 0 | — | `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`; inspect typed outcome |
1166	| SIGINT before / after settle | interrupted 130 / settled class | — | after-settle is never reclassified |
1167	
1168	The exact class/detail pairing is determined by the golden observation and
1169	closed schemas. Disclosure-only success details do not imply a clean doctor
1170	report or grant authority. No new D9 family is introduced.

135	## 1. Supported native cells (AR-13)
136	
137	### 1.1 Cell coordinates
138	
139	A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
140	matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`, validated by
141	`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`; its `cells` array is the **complete product** of its
142	own `capabilities` and `languageModes`, and the reference checks hold it to
143	exactly that product rather than to a number written here. (A literal count in
144	this prose said `60` while the matrix held 66; a second hand-maintained counter
145	would only go stale again, so the count is derived from the two arrays and
146	reported by the checks instead of restated.) Platform families are exactly the
147	four `platformId`
148	values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
149	`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
150	*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit

151	(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
152	by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.
153	
154	Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
155	qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
156	never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).

158	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
159	
160	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
161	|---|---|---|---|
162	| `ts-tsconfig` | `tsconfig.json` at the unit root (or named by discovery), `allowJs` absent/false | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=tsconfig` | JavaScript files are not program roots; a JS import target is `unresolved-module-specifier`. |
163	| `js-allowjs` | `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` with effective `allowJs=true` (jsconfig defaults `allowJs=true`) | `typescript-v2`, `allowJs=true` | `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` are program roots. |
164	| `js-synthesized` | Inside a `tsjs` unit already discovered by §1.4 U-1: no `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` at the unit root, so the `package.json` marker selects this mode. `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` files under that unit are program roots; they do not themselves make a unit | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=synthesized`, `synthesizerVersion=1` | Host synthesizes `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (§2.2); Plan-bound with `DEFAULTED` provenance, disclosed in output. |
165	| `rust-cargo` | `Cargo.toml` at the unit root (package or workspace) | `rust-v2` | Requires a sealed `DependencySourceSetV1` when the lock lists any non-path package (§3). |
166	| `rust-cargo-prepared` | as above, plus an admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3` of inert rows | `rust-v2` with `preparedOutputSetId` non-null | Expansions and directives are consumed as data; a site without a row is an unresolved edge (§3.6). |
167	| `syntax-only` | any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar | `syntax-v2` (grammar-only; no compiler) | Inventory/syntax/clones only; semantic rungs `language-tier-unsupported`. |
168	
169	**This table selects a MODE; it does not discover units.** No Recognition cell
170	mints a unit. For the five rows that name a **compilation** universe —
171	`ts-tsconfig`, `js-allowjs`, `js-synthesized`, `rust-cargo` and
172	`rust-cargo-prepared` — the cell is read **after** §1.4 U-1 has yielded a unit of
173	that language family, because those modes describe a program and a program needs
174	one. **`syntax-only` carries no such prerequisite and must not be read as if it
175	did:** it is the compiler-free path, it has no compilation unit at all (§1.2's
176	third-universe paragraph and §6.3's grammar dialect branch both depend on that),
177	and it is exactly what serves a repository in which U-1 yields **no** TS or Rust
178	unit. A file reached that way is `syntax-only` membership with `unitOrdinal: null`
179	under U-4, not a member of an invented unit. U-1 is the specific model — the closed `WorkspaceUnitV2` record,
180	the exactly-once `FileMembershipRowV1` law and the marker precedence
181	`tsconfig.json` > `jsconfig.json` > `package.json` — and a `tsjs` unit exists only
182	where a directory holds one of those three markers. So a directory of bare `.js`
183	files with no marker is **not** a unit: under U-4 each such file is
184	`syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language`, never a program member,
185	and no `js-synthesized` program is minted for them. An
186	earlier wording of the `js-synthesized` row read as an independent recognition
187	test ("`package.json` present **or** any `.js` file under the unit"), and an
188	implementer taking it alone would have minted units for bare-`.js` directories,
189	changing unit membership and therefore the Plan. The disjunct was never reachable
190	under U-1 — with no `tsconfig.json`, no `jsconfig.json` and no `package.json`
191	there is no unit for a `.js` file to be "under" — and the cell now says what it
192	always meant: within a U-1 unit whose marker is `package.json`, `.js` files are
193	program roots.
194	
195	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
196	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
197	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
198	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
199	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
200	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
201	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
202	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
203	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
204	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
205	
206	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
207	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
208	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
209	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
210	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
211	
212	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
213	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
214	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
215	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
216	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
217	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
218	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
219	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
220	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
221	  semantics the mode never computes.
222	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
223	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
224	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
225	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
226	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
227	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
228	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
229	  as a resolution claim.
230	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
231	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
232	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
233	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
234	  suffix must map to one grammar
235	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
236	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
237	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
238	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
239	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
240	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
241	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
242	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
243	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
244	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
245	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
246	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
247	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
248	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
249	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
250	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
251	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
252	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
253	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
254	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
255	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
256	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
257	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
258	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
259	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
260	
261	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
262	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
263	
264	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
265	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
266	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
267	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
268	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
269	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
270	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
271	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
272	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
273	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
274	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
275	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
276	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
277	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
278	
279	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
280	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
281	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
282	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
283	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
284	languages instead of ignoring four.
285	
286	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
287	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
288	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
289	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
290	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
291	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
292	
293	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
294	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
295	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
296	
297	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
298	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
299	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
300	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored

301	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
302	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
303	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
304	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
305	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
306	whether facts happen to exist:
307	
308	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
309	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
310	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
311	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
312	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
313	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
314	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
315	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
316	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
317	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
318	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
319	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
320	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
321	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
322	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
323	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
324	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
325	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
326	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
327	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
328	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
329	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
330	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
331	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
332	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
333	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
334	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
335	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
336	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
337	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
338	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
339	  exactly as the matrix already says.
340	
341	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
342	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
343	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
344	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
345	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
346	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
347	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
348	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
349	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
350	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
351	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
352	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
353	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
354	
355	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
356	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
357	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
358	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
359	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
360	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
361	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
362	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
363	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
364	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
365	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
366	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
367	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
368	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
369	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
370	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
371	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
372	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
373	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
374	cross-universe defect.
375	
376	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
377	**not** contain is owed nothing —
378	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
379	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
380	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
381	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
382	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
383	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
384	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
385	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
386	row, and never inferred. This is the specific rule that identity §3's "partition
387	the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions" defers to: the **disjointness**
388	half is general, applies within the full owning
389	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` tuple, and is
390	decided at retained Run closure against the registry's own
391	`coveragePartitionLaw`; the **omission** half is discharged only where this
392	registry carries a `coverageTotality` row. For the nine `symbol`-kind relations it
393	carries none, and the reason is the trust boundary stated below — symbol-to-file
394	attribution is not re-derivable from the retained Run — so no fact-per-symbol
395	obligation exists there. Evaluator3 separately requires the selected symbol
396	inventory and accounts for required work over its independently retained census
397	(identity §4). A symbol may have no call/reference fact, while a whole expected
398	inventory or work partition cannot silently disappear. Disjointness still applies, because it
399	asks a different question: not what was examined, but whether one interpretation
400	claimed a subject twice.
401	
402	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
403	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
404	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
405	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
406	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
407	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
408	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
409	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
410	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
411	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
412	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
413	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
414	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
415	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
416	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
417	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
418	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
419	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
420	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
421	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
422	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
423	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
424	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
425	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
426	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
427	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
428	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
429	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
430	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
431	
432	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
433	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
434	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
435	
436	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
437	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
438	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
439	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
440	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
441	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
442	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
443	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
444	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
445	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
446	
447	This particular guard — the one decided by the **selected grammar rows** — is
448	**syntax-universe specific**. Every *semantic* capability of the TypeScript and
449	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
450	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in

451	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
452	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
453	compiler-ownership obligation.
454	
455	It is **not** the only scope-capability guard, and an earlier revision of this
456	paragraph read as if it were. A separate and weaker law, stated in §10 and
457	published as
458	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/scopeCapabilityLaw`, applies
459	to **any** universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table — TypeScript and
460	the syntax universe both — and asks only whether a scoped path's own suffix
461	selects a variant in the table that universe published. For the syntax universe
462	that condition is strictly weaker than the grammar law above and is implied by
463	it, because the capability registry's `data-document` class law already states
464	that **no suffix of a data grammar appears in the syntax dialect table**. For
465	TypeScript it is the *only* such law, and it is what a `clones` scope over
466	`package.json` is now answered by. Which guard reaches a given scope first,
467	however, is decided by what each boundary can see, not by which law is stronger.
468	The suffix law needs nothing but the scope's own paths, so the native Coverage
469	producer boundary already applies it to the one case it can judge from a single
470	record — a `source-path` relation carrying a body-identity join, which is
471	`clones` — whenever the caller hands it the owning universe's dialect, as Run
472	closure does. Closure runs that producer admission **before** any of its own
473	prerequisites, so a false claim of complete Coverage for a `clones` scope over
474	a path no dialect table lists is refused there, as a producer-admission failure
475	naming the source variant, before the grammar guard. The grammar law is neither weakened nor reordered: among
476	closure's own prerequisites it is still applied ahead of the suffix backstop,
477	and it remains the sole owner, under its own refusal names, of everything a
478	suffix table cannot see — the `symbol` relations, the other syntax relations,
479	and the selection case where a path's suffix *is* in the table but no selected
480	grammar row owns it. An honestly disclosed unsupported scope still carries
481	`coverage: unknown` and the published `language-tier-unsupported` /
482	`capability-missing` pair. A false claim of complete Coverage is rejected; its
483	internal first-refusal name depends on which admission boundary detects it.
484	
485	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
486	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
487	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
488	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
489	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
490	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
491	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
492	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
493	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
494	supported one.
495	
496	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
497	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
498	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
499	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
500	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating
501	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
502	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
503	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
504	scope therefore remains admissible.
505	
506	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
507	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
508	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
509	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
510	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
511	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
512	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
513	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
514	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
515	
516	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
517	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
518	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
519	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
520	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
521	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
522	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
523	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
524	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.
525	
526	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
527	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
528	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
529	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

554	Limitations (closed ids; each is disclosed in Coverage, never hidden):
555	
556	- **L-JS1** synthesized options: `paths`/`baseUrl`/`rootDirs`/custom `types` are unknown; a specifier resolvable only through them is `unresolved-module-specifier`.
557	- **L-JS2** dynamic forms: computed member access, non-literal `require`/`import()`, indirect `eval`, reflective access and `any`-typed calls produce unresolved edges; resolution completeness for universal negatives is then `incomplete` (§4).
558	- **L-JS3** JavaScript types without annotation or JSDoc are `compiler-inferred` (§4.8). They are exact under the admitted universe and carry no probabilistic confidence; a rule pack that wants declared types uses `derivationPolicy=declared-only`.
559	- **L-RS1** external crates: every non-path package in `Cargo.lock` that unified feature resolution activates for the target must be present in the sealed dependency source set; otherwise the dependent crate's semantic rungs are `input-closure-incomplete` (§3.5). Syntax rungs remain complete.
560	- **L-RS2** dynamic dispatch and generics: `dyn Trait` calls resolve to the trait method declaration and are recorded as `trait-object-dynamic-dispatch` unresolved edges; generic bound calls as `generic-bound-dispatch`. Both count against resolution completeness for universal negatives.
561	- **L-RS3** non-prepared generated code: procedural-macro and build-script outputs are absent; each external proc-macro invocation site is a `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge and each package with a build script contributes `build-script-generated-unavailable`. `types@checked` on items whose type depends on such generated code is `unknown` with `input-closure-incomplete` (cause `generated-output-unavailable`). Declarative `macro_rules!` expansion is compiler-native and fully supported.

563	- **L-FW1** entry points: `reachability` universal negatives need an origin set; without a recognized framework or explicit origins they are `resolution-incomplete` with class `entry-point-unrecognized` (§8).

571	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
572	share a root.

575	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root

1062	
1063	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
1064	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
1065	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
1066	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
1067	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
1068	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
1069	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
1070	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
1071	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.

1073	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.

1099	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
1100	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
1101	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
1102	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
1103	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
1104	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
1105	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
1106	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
1107	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
1108	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
1109	never an ADMIT. It refuses when

1112	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;

1250	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
1251	
1252	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
1253	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
1254	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
1255	own language and refuses the other.
1256	
1257	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
1258	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
1259	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
1260	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
1261	
1262	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
1263	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
1264	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
1265	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
1266	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
1267	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
1268	descriptor and tree.
1269	
1270	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
1271	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
1272	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
1273	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
1274	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
1275	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
1276	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
1277	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
1278	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
1279	
1280	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
1281	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
1282	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).

1284	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
1285	
1286	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
1287	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
1288	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
1289	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.

1291	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
1292	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
1293	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.

1295	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
1296	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
1297	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
1298	
1299	| Field | Produced from |
1300	|---|---|
1301	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
1302	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
1303	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
1304	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. 1305	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` **names** the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must map to a retained component under the published name-to-component join below. These are `lib` names (`es2022`), never declaration-file names |
1306	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1307	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1308	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). 1313	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1314	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1315	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1316	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1317	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1318	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1319	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1320	
1321	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1322	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1323	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1324	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1325	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1326	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1327	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1328	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1329	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1330	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1331	divergence, not implementation freedom.
1332	
1333	| Rule | Statement |
1334	|---|---|
1335	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1336	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1337	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1338	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1339	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1340	
1341	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1342	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1343	
1344	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1345	|---|---|---|---|
1346	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1347	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1348	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1349	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1350

1351	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1352	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1353	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1354	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1355	
1356	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1357	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1358	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1359	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1360	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1361	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1362	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1363	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1364	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1365	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1366	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1367	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1368	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1369	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1370	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1371	
1372	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1373	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1374	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1375	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1376	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1377	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1378	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1379	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1380	which two paths share a basename refuses
1381	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1382	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1383	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1384	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1385	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1386	
1387	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1388	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1389	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1390	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1391	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1392	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1393	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1394	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).

1397	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1398	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1399	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1400	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1401	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.

1403	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1404	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context

1409	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to

1411	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.

1413	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`

1470	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1471	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1472	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1473	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1474	
1475	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1476	
1477	| Field | Rule |
1478	|---|---|
1479	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1480	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1481	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1482	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1483	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |

1489	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1490	
1491	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1492	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1493	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1494	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1495	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1496	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1497	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1498	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1499	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1500	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.

1501	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1502	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1503	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1504	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1505	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1506	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1507	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1508	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1509	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1510	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1511	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1512	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1513	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1514	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1515	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1516	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1517	  syntax analysis.
1518	
1519	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1520	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1521	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1522	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

1696	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1697	
1698	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1699	
1700	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1701	
1702	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1703	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1704	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1705	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1706	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1707	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1708	
1709	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1710	
1711	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1712	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1713	
1714	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1715	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1716	
1717	```
1718	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1719	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1720	```
1721	
1722	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1723	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1724	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1725	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1726	
1727	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1728	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1729	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1730	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1731	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1732	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1733	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1734	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1735	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1736	
1737	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1738	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1739	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1740	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1741	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1742	against a value the provider never supplied.
1743	
1744	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1745	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1746	
1747	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1748	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1749	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1750	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1751	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1752	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1753	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1754	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1755	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1756	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1757	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1758	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1759	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1760	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1761	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1762	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1763	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1764	
1765	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1766	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1767	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1768	
1769	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1770	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1771	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1772	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1773	
1774	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1775	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1776	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1777	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1778	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1779	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1780	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
1781

2081	
2082	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
2083	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.
2084	
2085	1. Relation absent from the view → `required-relation-missing`.
2086	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.

2095	`partial-ok` passes step 5 vacuously but still runs steps 1–4 and 8: the former

2167	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
2168	
2169	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
2170	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2171	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
2172	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
2173	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
2174	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
2175	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
2176	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
2177	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2178	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2179	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2180	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.
2181	
2182	**The two clauses have different scopes, and the second is deliberately the wider
2183	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2184	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2185	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only
2186	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2187	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2188	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2189	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2190	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It
2191	is not read as types-scoped, and reading it that way would be a *weakening* — it
2192	would permit a native `clones` or `references` provider to emit a fabricated
2193	percentage, which is exactly what §4.8 removed.

2402	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
2403	
2404	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
2405	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
2406	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
2407	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
2408	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
2409	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
2410	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
2411	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
2412	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
2413	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
2414	
2415	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
2416	|---|---|---|---|
2417	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
2418	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
2419	
2420	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
2421	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
2422	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.

2428	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
2429	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:

3173	**A refused value can exceed the diagnostic bound, and the projection is
3174	bounded.** `DomainDetail.subject` is `BoundedText` (1024) while a *structurally
3175	valid* `languageMode` may be 4096 characters; the composed subject then reached
3176	4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at
3177	`termination.domainDetail.subject` or `errors[0].subject`. `bounded_subject`
3178	elides: the registered **key** is preserved verbatim — it selects the code, the
3179	class and the origin — and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading
3180	window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. Emitting the untruncated
3181	string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and
3182	reclassifying the input error as success would be false. The code, class and
3183	origin are never changed by the elision.
3184	
3185	The encoding is normative, and its **units** are stated because they differ
3186	between the two operations. Let `raw` be the composed subject
3187	`<registered key>[:<value>]` as an **admitted Unicode scalar string**. Length and
3188	slicing count **Unicode code points**, which is what `BoundedText`'s JSON Schema
3189	`maxLength` counts — not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units. If
3190	`len(raw) ≤ 1024` the subject **is** `raw`. Otherwise it is
3191	
3192	```
3193	raw[: 1024 − len("...#sha256:") − 64] + "...#sha256:" + hex(SHA256(raw.encode("utf-8")))
3194	```
3195	
3196	— the marker `...#sha256:` is ASCII, the digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex
3197	characters, the SHA-256 input is exactly `raw` encoded as UTF-8 with **no**
3198	additional normalization, and the result is exactly 1024 code points. A
3199	non-ASCII value therefore has a UTF-8 byte length that may exceed 1024 while its
3200	scalar length does not, and the two operations must not be conflated.
3201	
3202	Two distinct long values are distinguished under the **ordinary
3203	collision-resistance assumption** for SHA-256; this is not a claim that collision
3204	is impossible. **The guarantee is confined to what is published** — the bounded
3205	subject and its digest. This contract does **not** promise a separate retained
3206	store of the untruncated value and names none; a host that keeps its own
3207	operational log may match it by recomputing this digest, which is why the digest
3208	is published at all.

3211	guards emit `native.requested-capability-unregistered:made-up-capability` and

3554	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
3555	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
3556	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
3557	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
3558	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
3559	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
3560	make it so.
3561	
3562	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
3563	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
3564	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
3565	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
3566	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
3567	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
3568	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
3569	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
3570	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
3571	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
3572	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
3573	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
3574	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
3575	
3576	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
3577	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
3578	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
3579	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
3580	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
3581	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
3582	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
3583	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
3584	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
3585	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
3586	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
3587	
3588	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
3589	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
3590	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
3591	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
3592	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.
3593	This record states what a producer claims it enumerated; it admits no compiler,
3594	measures no build and qualifies no enumerator.
3595
